answer: Plant honeypot tasks whose answers are deliberately wrong and score every recruit on them, because a scripted farm copies the nectar every time while a real worker flags the trap. One caught recruit burns its inviter's quota and its whole referral ripple, so the cheap route dies: a farmer pays for 200 identities, gets 30 flagged as honeypots and watches the rest spiral into manual review, where 40 task-hours of human checking cost more than the farm could ever earn.
